rationale: Surfaced by the 024 US5 de-suppression, which narrowed `drop_absent_optional` to deacon's side. While the rule ran on BOTH sides, an authored null, an authored empty collection and an omitted property all normalized to 'the key is absent on both sides', so the three FR-055 states produced ONE observation and the difference could not be seen. With the rule confined to the side whose serializer defect it compensates, the reference's faithful echo survives and the difference is visible. Measured at oracle 0.87.0. UPDATED BY #398, which applied `skip_serializing_if` to every `Option<_>` field on `DevContainerConfig`: the tolerated set changed shape and grew by one, and both movements are deliberate. `configuration.forwardPorts` and `configuration.containerEnv` still diverge (the author wrote `[]`/`{}`, the reference echoes them, and deacon emits the same bytes it would emit unauthored), because those two are among the 11 fields still typed as bare collections rather than `Option`. `nullEmptyOmitted.mounts` still diverges for the same reason, stated positively on a property the document does not author. NEW: `configuration.name` and `nullEmptyOmitted.name` now diverge, where before the fix both CLIs emitted `null` and AGREED — deacon holds an authored null and an omission in the same `None`, so omitting unauthored optionals necessarily omits authored nulls too. That boundary moved rather than closed, which the pre-fix version of this waiver predicted in as many words. Net: deacon went from ~40 unconditionally emitted keys to 13, and the residual is one schema-invalid input shape. This remains a fidelity DEFECT, not a design choice, tracked at #398 with the remaining scope named there. Scoped to the named paths on the one case authored to demonstrate them; self-invalidates the moment a difference stops reproducing.
